title: A four-point DFT by hand
instructions:
## Frequencies in four samples

The signal x = [1, 0, −1, 0] was sampled at fs = 8000 Hz. Its DFT is X[k] = Σ x[n]·e^(−j2πkn/N) with N = 4.

1. |X[0]| (the DC term).
2. |X[1]|.
3. The frequency resolution (bin spacing) in Hz.
4. The frequency of bin k = 1 in Hz.
5. The Nyquist frequency.
6. How many samples one period of a 1 kHz tone occupies at this sampling rate.
hints: X[0] is simply the sum of the samples.
For k = 1 the twiddles are 1, −j, −1, j: X[1] = 1 − (−1)(−1)·… work it through: 1·1 + 0 + (−1)·(−1) + 0 = 2.
Bin spacing = fs / N; Nyquist = fs / 2.

checks.label: Samples per period of 1 kHz
checks.question: Samples in one period of a 1 kHz tone at 8 kHz:

realityNote: x is one period of a 2 kHz cosine sampled four times, which is why all its energy sits in bins 1 and 3. A 1024-point FFT at 8 kHz gives bins 7.8 Hz apart, the resolution of a basic spectrum analyser app.
